screening_decisions.reason: This is a theoretical/conceptual paper discussing the relationship between social learning theory and the Health Belief Model. It does not report a randomised controlled trial, nor does it involve any intervention with personalised risk communication for screening. It is purely a theoretical discussion.

This is an editorial/opinion piece publishing a letter and response about concerns regarding the NHS breast screening programme. It is not a randomised controlled trial and does not test any intervention with personalised risk communication.

This is a randomised controlled trial (N=279) comparing standard care vs an educational intervention designed to help women understand their personal family history of cancer and inherited risk. The intervention provides personalised risk information. Outcomes include knowledge, perceived risk, and intention to obtain genetic testing (cognitive and behavioural outcomes). While focused on genetic testing rather than traditional screening, it involves personalised risk communication and decision-making about health services, warranting inclusion pending full-text review.

This is a historical/theoretical paper describing the development of the Health Belief Model. It is not a randomised controlled trial and does not test any intervention with personalised risk communication for screening.
This is an overview/review paper discussing concepts, models and methods concerning risk analysis and decision making. It is not a randomised controlled trial and does not test any intervention.

This is a prospective randomised trial (N=200) comparing individualized breast cancer risk counseling to general health counseling. The intervention provides personalised risk communication (individualized breast cancer risk counseling). Outcomes include risk comprehension (cognitive outcome) and addresses psychological aspects (affective outcomes). The study focuses on women with family history of breast cancer considering screening/testing. Meets key criteria for inclusion.

This is a study protocol describing the design and methods of the BRISC study. It does not report results or outcomes from the intervention. Without reported outcomes, it cannot be assessed against the selection criteria requiring measures of informed decisions and cognitive, affective, or behavioural outcomes.

This is a methodology chapter from the Cochrane Handbook describing tools for assessing risk of bias in clinical trials. It is not a randomised controlled trial and does not test any intervention with personalised risk communication.

This is a prospective randomised study with 2x2 factorial design (N=1,367) comparing tailored telephone counseling, tailored mailed materials, combination, vs usual care for mammography screening. The interventions are tailored/personalised based on the Transtheoretical and Health Belief Models. Outcomes include mammography status (behavioural) and beliefs/knowledge (cognitive). Meets criteria for personalised risk communication intervention for screening with relevant outcomes.

This is a randomised trial (N=176) evaluating personalized Colon Cancer Risk Counseling (CCRC) sessions with print materials and follow-up phone calls compared to General Health Counseling. The intervention provides personalised risk communication for colorectal cancer screening. Outcomes include screening adherence (behavioural) and participant ratings of information usefulness (cognitive). Meets key criteria for inclusion.

This is a randomised trial comparing an in-person tailored intervention to routine care for mammography screening. The intervention is targeted toward perceived risk, benefits, and barriers to breast cancer screening (personalised risk communication elements). Outcome is adoption of mammography (behavioural). While the abstract is brief, it appears to meet criteria for a personalised intervention for screening with behavioural outcomes.
This is a systematic review, not a randomised controlled trial. The selection criteria specifically require RCTs. Reviews are excluded from this screening process.

This is a randomised controlled trial (N=5,686) comparing a risk appraisal questionnaire (that determines individual risk of coronary heart disease) plus health questionnaire vs health questionnaire alone. The intervention provides personalised risk communication through the risk appraisal. Outcome is rate of cholesterol testing (behavioural). Meets criteria for personalised risk communication intervention for screening with behavioural outcomes.

This is an opinion/position paper discussing policy issues around screening information and informed choice. It is not a randomised controlled trial and does not test any intervention with personalised risk communication.

This is a large randomised trial (N=4,014) comparing four conditions including tailored print materials (single and multiple mailouts) vs untailored control. The intervention provides personalised/tailored risk communication based on baseline information. Outcome is colorectal cancer screening uptake (behavioural). Meets criteria for personalised risk communication intervention for screening with behavioural outcomes.

This is a randomised trial comparing a stepped-intensity intervention (mailings, telephone calls, and counseling if appropriate given genetic risk) to delayed treatment control. The intervention includes personalised elements (counseling based on genetic risk). Outcomes include mammography uptake (behavioural), quality of life, knowledge, and cancer worry (cognitive/affective). Meets criteria for intervention with personalised elements for screening with relevant outcomes.

This is a randomised controlled trial (N=1,577) comparing evidence-based risk information brochure with interactive internet modules vs official information leaflet for colorectal cancer screening. The primary outcome is explicitly "informed choice" comprising knowledge, attitude, and uptake. Secondary outcomes include knowledge and uptake. This is a strong match for the selection criteria with explicit measurement of informed decisions and cognitive/behavioural outcomes.

This is a psychometric validation study evaluating the properties of a decisional conflict scale. It is not a randomised controlled trial testing an intervention with personalised risk communication. It evaluates a measurement tool rather than an intervention effect.

This is an expert opinion/recommendations paper offering best practices for conveying health risks. It is not a randomised controlled trial and does not test any intervention. It discusses existing evidence but does not present primary research data.

This is a randomised controlled trial (N=278) comparing a Colorectal Cancer Risk Appraisal (personalised risk assessment) to a simple information letter for fecal occult blood testing. The intervention provides personalised risk communication. Outcomes include FOB test compliance (behavioural) and intention to get FOB test (cognitive/behavioural). Meets criteria for personalised risk communication intervention for screening with behavioural outcomes.
This is a protocol for a Cochrane Review, not a primary randomised controlled trial. It describes objectives for a future systematic review rather than reporting original RCT data.
This is an editorial/news article about an independent review being conducted, not a randomised controlled trial. No intervention or outcomes are reported.

While this is an RCT with tailored interventions for colorectal cancer screening, it only reports cost-effectiveness and screening uptake outcomes. There are no measures of informed decisions (knowledge, risk perception accuracy, decisional conflict, or informed choice).
This RCT tests a tailored computer intervention for mammography screening but only reports screening uptake as the outcome. No measures of informed decisions are reported.

This study examines women already attending a surveillance program, not individuals deciding whether to undergo screening. The intervention focuses on improving risk perception after enrollment rather than supporting the initial screening decision. No informed decision measures are reported.
This is a conceptual/theoretical paper exploring risk communication strategies, not a randomised controlled trial. No empirical data or intervention outcomes are reported.

This is an RCT testing a decision aid (Ottawa Personal Decision Guide) for prenatal testing decisions. It measures decisional conflict (a measure of informed decision quality). While prenatal testing is diagnostic rather than traditional screening, it involves similar decision-making processes about whether to undergo testing. Conservative approach suggests inclusion for full-text review.

This RCT compares tailored vs non-tailored print materials for BRCA genetic testing. It reports knowledge improvement and risk perception accuracy - both critical components of informed decision making. The tailored materials constitute personalised risk communication. BRCA testing serves a screening function for high-risk individuals.

This RCT tests tailored CRC risk factor feedback with social comparison for colorectal cancer screening. It reports cognitive outcomes (perceived risks, ambivalence) and behavioral outcomes (screening intentions, FOBT completion) addressing the screening decision. These outcomes are relevant to informed decision making.

This RCT evaluates a shared decision-making program for treatment decisions in men with benign prostatic hyperplasia. This is a treatment decision, not a screening decision. The study does not involve screening procedures.

This RCT tests individually tailored messages for mammography screening but only reports compliance and stage of adoption outcomes. No measures of informed decisions (knowledge, risk perception, decisional conflict, or informed choice) are reported.

This RCT tests individualized health education for cervical cancer screening. While it reports knowledge and Pap smear rates, it does not report measures of informed decisions (such as decisional conflict, informed choice, or risk perception accuracy).
This is a review article discussing risk communication framing strategies, not a randomised controlled trial. No primary data or intervention outcomes are reported.

This RCT tests a decision aid with quantitative risk information for bowel cancer screening. It directly measures informed choice (adequate knowledge and consistency between attitudes and behavior) as a main outcome, along with knowledge, attitudes, screening participation, and decisional conflict. This is a strong match for all selection criteria.
This is a telephone survey examining how benefit framing affects screening decisions, not a randomised controlled trial. The study design does not meet the RCT criterion.
This is an opinion piece/commentary calling for a shift in approach to cancer screening. It is not a randomised controlled trial and reports no empirical data.

This RCT tests tailored vs standardized mammography recommendation letters. While it reports letter recall and mammography status, it does not report measures of informed decisions (knowledge, risk perception accuracy, decisional conflict, or informed choice).
This is an editorial discussing benefits and harms of mammography screening, not a randomised controlled trial. No primary data or intervention outcomes are reported.
This is a systematic review and meta-analysis of the emotional impact of screening, not a primary randomised controlled trial. While it synthesizes RCT data, it is not itself an RCT.
This is a literature review searching for systematic reviews on informed choice and screening, not a randomised controlled trial. No primary data or intervention outcomes are reported.

This is a meta-analytic review, not a randomised controlled trial. The study synthesizes 57 existing studies rather than conducting a primary RCT with personalised risk communication for screening decisions.

This appears to be a Cochrane systematic review (based on title and cochranelibrary.com reference), not a primary randomised controlled trial. The abstract is incomplete and does not describe an RCT intervention.

While this is an RCT about colorectal cancer screening, the intervention is general health education, not personalised risk communication. The study does not report measures of informed decisions, only compliance rates.

This is a randomized study using the Gail model for personalised breast cancer risk assessment (personalised risk communication element). It addresses screening procedures (BSE, CBE, mammography) and reports behavioral outcomes (adherence, confidence). While informed decision measures are not explicitly stated, the study involves personalised risk communication for screening decisions.

This is an RCT with individually tailored messages (personalised risk communication) for mammography screening. It reports cognitive outcomes (belief variables) and behavioral outcomes (mammography compliance). The intervention addresses the decision to undergo screening.
While this is an RCT with tailored materials, it focuses on weight-loss behavior, not screening procedures. The study does not address screening decisions or screening-related outcomes.
This is a methodological paper about the GRADE system for rating evidence quality, not a randomised controlled trial. It does not involve personalised risk communication or screening interventions.

This is a methodological paper describing a risk projection model, not a randomised controlled trial. It presents a method for calculating individualized probabilities but does not test an intervention with outcomes.
This is a literature review about risk communication outcomes, not a randomised controlled trial. It reviews existing research rather than conducting a primary RCT.

This is an RCT with individual genetic risk counseling (personalised risk communication) for breast cancer genetic testing (screening procedure). It reports cognitive outcomes (beliefs about testing) and behavioral outcomes (interest in testing). The intervention addresses the decision to undergo screening/testing.

This is an RCT with risk-tailored messages (personalised risk communication) for mammography screening. It reports behavioral outcomes (mammography rates) and addresses the decision to undergo screening. The study explicitly tests personalised risk communication for screening decisions.

This is an RCT with tailored print pamphlets and counseling (personalised risk communication) for colorectal cancer screening. It reports behavioral outcomes (screening adherence) and cognitive outcomes (decisional balance). The intervention addresses the decision to undergo screening.

This is an RCT with counseling interventions for mammography screening. It reports cognitive outcomes (perception of susceptibility, knowledge, barriers, benefits) and behavioral outcomes (mammography adherence). While the personalisation element is less clear, the counseling addresses screening decisions.
This is a theoretical paper about the Elaboration Likelihood model of persuasion, not a randomised controlled trial. It discusses political messages, not health screening interventions.

This is an RCT with a decision aid providing detailed absolute risk and benefit information (personalised risk communication) for colorectal cancer screening. It explicitly reports informed choice measures (20.9% vs 5.8% informed), knowledge, and screening decisions. This clearly meets all selection criteria.

This is a cluster RCT with a decision aid (personalised risk communication) for prenatal screening tests. It explicitly reports informed choice measures (76% vs 65% informed), knowledge, and decisional conflict. This clearly meets all selection criteria.

This is an RCT with tailored message pages (personalised risk communication) for colorectal cancer screening. It reports behavioral outcomes (screening rates) and addresses the decision to undergo screening. The study explicitly tests tailored interventions for screening decisions.
This is a methodology chapter describing meta-analysis procedures, not a randomised controlled trial. It does not involve personalised risk communication or screening interventions.
This is an opinion piece/commentary about breast cancer screening debate, not a randomised controlled trial. It does not test an intervention with personalised risk communication.

This is a systematic review updating evidence for the USPSTF, not a randomised controlled trial. It synthesizes existing RCTs rather than conducting a primary RCT with personalised risk communication.
Not an RCT - this is an ethical analysis/opinion piece examining whether current cervical screening practices are unethical. No intervention is being tested.
Not an RCT and not about health screening - this is a general hazard management article discussing nuclear power plants, food safety, and environmental risks, not medical screening procedures.
Not an RCT - this is a theoretical/conceptual paper outlining a framework for investigating patient decision making, not an empirical trial.

RCT with individualized breast cancer risk counseling (personalised risk communication) for mammography screening. Reports behavioral outcomes (mammography use). While informed decision measures are not explicitly mentioned in the abstract, the study warrants full-text review to confirm if such measures were collected.
Not an RCT - this is a theoretical overview paper describing the transtheoretical model of health behavior change, not an empirical intervention trial.
Not an RCT (repeated measures pilot study) and focuses on treatment decisions (medical therapy vs angioplasty vs bypass surgery) for diagnosed heart disease, not screening decisions.

RCT with personalized counseling approach for BRCA1 genetic testing (screening). Reports knowledge (cognitive), perceived risk/benefits/limitations (affective/cognitive), and testing intentions (behavioral) - all measures of informed decision making. Meets all selection criteria.
Not an RCT - this is a critical analysis and mathematical modelling paper about public health policy tensions, not an intervention trial for screening.
Not an RCT - this is a systematic review of measures used in informed decision making studies, not a primary intervention trial.
Not an RCT - this is a conceptual/methodological paper discussing how to measure informed choice in cancer screening, not an intervention trial.
Not an RCT - this is a longitudinal before-and-after study without randomization. While it involves personalized risk information for breast cancer, the study design does not meet the RCT criterion.
Not an RCT - this is an ethical analysis paper examining the ethics of clinical guidelines, not an intervention trial.
Not an RCT - this is a methodological paper about efficient literature searching strategies for systematic reviews, not an intervention trial.

RCT with individually-tailored behavior change information (personalised risk communication) via enhanced HRA. Reports behavioral outcomes including cholesterol screening, mammography, and Pap smear use. Warrants full-text review to confirm informed decision measures.

RCT with breast cancer risk counseling intervention (personalised risk communication) for sexual minority women. Reports affective outcomes (perceived risk, anxieties, fears) and behavioral outcomes (breast screening rates). Warrants full-text review for informed decision measures.
Not an RCT - this is a content analysis of 58 pamphlets about breast cancer screening, not an intervention trial.

RCT with tailored intervention (personalised risk communication) for skin cancer screening among melanoma family members. Reports behavioral outcomes (skin examinations, sun protection) and cognitive mediators (intentions, benefits, barriers, self-efficacy). Warrants full-text review for informed decision measures.
Not an RCT - this is a qualitative study using focus group interviews to explore GP attitudes toward shared decision making, not an intervention trial.

RCT with tailored behavioral intervention (personalised risk communication) for prostate cancer early detection/screening. Reports behavioral outcomes (adherence to screening) and cognitive outcomes (intentions). Warrants full-text review for informed decision measures.

RCT with personalized telephone counseling and tailored materials (personalised risk communication) for skin cancer screening among melanoma siblings. Reports behavioral outcomes (skin examinations, sunscreen use). Warrants full-text review for informed decision measures.

This study meets the selection criteria: (1) It is a randomized controlled trial; (2) It incorporates a tailored, interactive computer-delivered intervention which constitutes a personalised risk communication element; (3) The population consists of patients 50-70 years undergoing colorectal cancer screening procedures; (4) It reports cognitive outcomes (increased knowledge), affective outcomes (CRC screening self-efficacy), and behavioural outcomes (screening completion rates). While the abstract does not explicitly mention 'informed decision' measures, knowledge and self-efficacy are recognized components of informed decision-making. Following the conservative approach of including when uncertain, this study should be included for further review.

This study does not meet the selection criteria for multiple reasons: (1) It is NOT a randomized controlled trial - it is a scale development and validation study; (2) There is no intervention with a personalised risk communication element - the study focuses on developing and validating the Satisfaction with Decision (SWD) scale; (3) The context is not screening procedures - it was developed in the context of postmenopausal hormone-replacement therapy decisions and tested with flu shot intentions; (4) It does not report measures of informed decisions in the context of screening. This study is clearly outside the scope of the review protocol.
